chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shami, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, prohibited wine specifically, so its little and its much is forbidden, just as He prohibited the dead animal, and the blood, and the flesh of the pig; and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited the drink from every intoxicant; and whatever the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited, then indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prohibited it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on small and large quantities of wine and intoxicants in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the divine prohibition of *khamr* extends to all quantities, paralleling the status of *najis* items like meat and blood, while establishing the principle of *tawatur* between the Prophet’s prohibition of every intoxicant and Allah’s command. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for deriving the ruling of *khamr* as inherently impure and forbidden regardless of quantity, reinforcing the concept that the Prophet’s legislative authority is an extension of divine will.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid Bin Jareyr, from Abu Al Rabie Al Shamy who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Prohibited the wine particularly, therefore a little of it or a lot of it, is Prohibited, just as the dead, and the blood, and the flesh of the swine is Prohibited; and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> Prohibited the drinks from every intoxicant; and whatever Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> prohibited, so it is Prohibited by Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from abu al-Rabi’ al-Shamiy who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has made the very substance of wine unlawful, in a small or large quantity. It is unlawful just as dead animals, blood and pork are unlawful. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, made wine unlawful and all intoxicating liquor. Whatever the Messenger of Allah has made unlawful, Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, also has made it unlawful.’”
